text:
maria: Heads-up: scheduling a rolling maintenance tonight for eu-central2 between 01:00-03:30 UTC. We're swapping a subset of BMCs and doing NIC firmware sanity on 6 racks. Affects: gpu-pool-eu2-priority (~120 GPUs), best-effort pools should be fine.

maria: Plan is staged drains 2 racks at a time, 20m cordon/drain + 10m reboot + warmup. Expected ~10-12% short-term capacity hit for 30-45m per cohort.

jake: Is there a backfill plan for longer jobs? any recommended cutoff for queued batch jobs?

maria: @jake yes — we want long jobs (>=6h) to be rescheduled to spot pools or to start after 04:30 UTC. Short jobs (<1h) can still land in priority pool with preemption risk. We'll add a soft quota bump on `gpu-pool-eu2-spot` to absorb ~30 GPUs.

anya: What's the fallback if the NIC swap causes transient egress blackholes? do we have cross-region routing to failover?

sam: We have automatic edge-failover to eu-west1 for model-serving routes, but data-plane affinity will cause higher latency. We'll enable traffic steering to eu-west1 for critical routes; non-critical inference will remain queued.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: ID mnt-eu2-202903. Window 2029-03-15T01:00:00Z -> 2029-03-15T03:30:00Z. Impact: rolling drain, possible 5-15% tail latency increase for a few minutes during rack rejoin.

pablo: Cost note — diverting to spot will increase token egress across regions and run up inter-region egress; estimate +$1.2k for the window if we push 40 GPUs worth of traffic to eu-west1. Also diffs in GPU type could affect perf.

maria: Agreed re: cost. Ops: prefer to migrate only what we must. We'll start with non-prod and low-traffic models, then move to prod if health looks stable.

sam: Canary steps I'm going to run at T+00:30: cordon two nodes in cohort-1, drain live-model pods, run perf smoke. If good, continue next cohort. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-eu2-03
kubectl drain gpu-node-eu2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
# warmup bench
python tools/bench_warmup.py --pool gpu-pool-eu2-priority --concurrency 4
```

jake: Sounds good. I'll hold non-urgent scheduled infra jobs starting 00:45 UTC and post status.

anya: Who's on-call for netops if we see persistent BGP flaps?

ops-lead: @anya @sam netops on-call is @pablo tonight. He has the escalation path to cloud provider NOC.

pablo: Yep I'm on-call. I'll be monitoring netflow and path changes; will trigger cross-region reroute if >3% packet loss for >5m.

maria: Final ask: please 👍 on this thread if you saw it and add any blockers. I'll post a short post-mortem template link after the window.

jake: 👍

anya: 👍

sam: 👍 running the canary at T+00:30

pablo: 👍 watching netops

infra-bot: Reminder: 45m before maintenance: run `infractl preflight mnt-eu2-202903` and verify `prefix-cache` warmup status.
